s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic swelling of the palate in an infant with a firm, nonmobile mass
salient_findings: Firm, nonmobile mass in the right posterior hard palate
Expansile lesion of the maxillary crest with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure
Thinning and perforation of the maxillary sinus walls and lateral displacement of the nasal cavity wall
key_facts: 10-month-old male infant
Asymptomatic swelling of the palate
Swelling first noticed several weeks earlier
No swelling noted at birth
Firm, nonmobile mass in the right posterior hard palate
Mass extends from the maxillary tuberosity medially almost to the midline
Expansile lesion of the maxillary crest with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure on CT
Thinning and perforation of the maxillary sinus walls
Lateral displacement of the nasal cavity wall

shortlist.label: Cemento-ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic findings of a well-defined, expansile lesion with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure match this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, nonmobile mass and radiographic findings of an expansile lesion could be consistent with fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Odontogenic myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Asymptomatic swelling and radiolucent areas on CT could suggest an odontogenic myxoma

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile lesion with thinning and perforation of the maxillary sinus walls could be seen in central giant cell granuloma

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral involvement is typical, but unilateral cases can occur, and the age of the patient could fit with cherubism

raw.rationale: The expansile lesion with mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure on CT and the location in the maxillary crest are consistent with a cemento-ossifying fibroma, which is a benign fibro-osseous lesion that can cause bone expansion and displacement of surrounding structures.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: While fibrous dysplasia can cause bone expansion, it typically has a ground-glass appearance on radiographs and is less likely to have a mixed radiolucent and radiopaque internal structure.

rejected.label: Odontogenic myxoma
rejected.why: Odontogenic myxoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the mandible and has a characteristic soap-bubble appearance on radiographs, which is not consistent with the findings in this case.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Central giant cell granuloma is a benign lesion that can cause bone expansion, but it typically has a more aggressive appearance on radiographs and is often associated with pain or tenderness, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cherubism
rejected.why: Cherubism is a rare genetic disorder that causes bilateral expansion of the mandible and maxilla, but it typically presents with bilateral involvement and has a more characteristic appearance on radiographs, which is not consistent with the findings in this case.
